bullets.title: S&P +0.4%, NDX futures hit session highs; broad market constructive despite VIX uptick
bullets.body: S&P 500 trading at 7,484 (+0.4%) with NDX futures extending gains to +1% session high. VIX rose 3.7% to 18.07 despite equity gains, reflecting cross-asset uncertainty from Middle East escalation. JPM maintains S&P YE2026 PT of $7,800 with FY26/27 EPS of $350/$390, favoring Quality Growth and direct AI exposure.

bullets.title: Iran-US conflict escalating: tanker explosions in Hormuz, Bahrain air nav attacked
bullets.body: Iran reported two tanker explosions in the Strait of Hormuz with ship traffic near standstill, while Bahrain confirmed Iranian attacks on civil air navigation systems (operations unaffected). Pentagon withheld information on dozens of US military injuries per NYT. Mediators proposed a 10-day strike pause to revive the Iran-US interim deal; ceasefire probability two-thirds, uncontrolled escalation to energy infrastructure ~one-third and rising.

bullets.title: Oil volatile: Brent +15% since ceasefire collapse, then falls below $87 intraday
bullets.body: Brent crude surged nearly 15% since the Middle East ceasefire ended earlier this month, but futures reversed sharply intraday with Brent falling below $87/barrel and WTI dropping 2.6% to session lows. US Strategic Petroleum Reserve sits at a 41-year low (lowest since April 1983). Morgan Stanley notes Europe's diesel refining margins at record highs driven by supply disruptions, not crude prices.

bullets.title: Hedgeye July inflation nowcast +3.40% y/y; core PCE June expected mild at +0.18% m/m
bullets.body: Hedgeye's July CPI nowcast is +3.40% y/y (up 3 bps from 7/17) but down 13 bps sequentially from June, with Middle East energy volatility the primary driver of trajectory uncertainty. Separately, PPI/CPI transposition models forecast June core PCE at +0.18% m/m (lowest since November) and +3.3% y/y, with headline PCE at -0.07% m/m. US inflation has been above the Fed's 2% target for 64 consecutive months averaging 4%/year since 2019.

bullets.title: Fed rhetoric hawkish but actions dovish; September hike still a coin flip
bullets.body: UBS flags Fed's verbal posture is more hawkish than actual policy actions. 22V notes core PCE implied at 0.2% MoM for July, below the 0.25% threshold that would trigger a July hike, making current tightening risk much lower; September hike remains a coin flip. 10-year yields expected to hover near 4.5%; Treasuries erased declines as WTI fell intraday.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex debate intensifies: JPM bullish ($730B 2026), Jefferies warns of capital destruction
bullets.body: JPM estimates hyperscalers will spend ~$730B in capex in 2026 and $900B+ in 2027, noting sufficient debt capacity (~$1.7T room), and that hyperscalers now account for 50%+ of S&P 500 capex. In contrast, Jefferies strategist Chris Wood warns of massive capital destruction risk as LLMs commoditize, token prices collapse, and hyperscalers accumulate $662B in off-balance-sheet data center lease commitments. A Fed study found no decisive evidence yet of AI productivity gains, and one analyst argues AI capex share of aggregate demand growth is well below half.

bullets.title: Kimi K3 launch triggers DeepSeek-redux debate: bullish for memory/GPU demand, bearish for AI lab moats
bullets.body: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 is viewed by UBS and Morgan Stanley as a DeepSeek R1-style moment — bullish for NVDA and MU as memory bottlenecks intensify (DC memory prices up 25%+ Q2-to-Q3), but bearish for proprietary AI lab economics as open-weight models close the performance gap. Kimi K3 is 50-70% more expensive per task than GPT-5.6 despite similar token pricing, and its scale-up networking requirements (rack-scale GPU infra exceeding 64 GPUs) likely increase HBM/NAND demand via Jevons Paradox. Trump administration is reportedly considering tougher restrictions on Chinese AI models following the launch.

bullets.title: AMD +5% on Microsoft Azure Helios deployment; each GW-scale customer worth $15-20B revenue
bullets.body: Microsoft announced deployment of AMD Helios Rackscale on Azure for frontier model AI inference, including MI455X GPUs, Venice CPUs, and Pensando networking — shipping H2 2026. Wolfe estimates OpenAI and Meta could be GW-scale Helios customers in CY27, with each GW of MI-400 capacity driving $15-20B revenue and $3-4 EPS impact. AMD is hosting Advancing AI Day on 7/23 with additional GPU deal hints.

bullets.title: TSMC CFO confirms additional $100B Arizona capex; semiconductor volumes dominate global trading
bullets.body: TSMC CFO Wendell Huang confirmed an additional $100B investment in US Arizona operations driven by structural AI chip demand, reaffirming confidence in profitable growth as long as the megatrend holds. Separately, 259 semiconductor companies now represent 20%+ of daily trading volumes globally despite comprising a small fraction of listed stocks.

bullets.title: Memory shortage intensifying: DC prices +25% Q2-to-Q3; Nvidia CMX to drive NAND surge 35M→100M+ TB
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Joe Moore, after purchasing checks, says data center memory shortages show no signs of abating with prices up at least 25% q/q. Nvidia CMX clusters (576 SSDs, 9,600 TB each) are projected to surge NAND demand from 35M TB this year to 100M+ TB next year. Samsung is expanding its Nvidia alliance into NAND flash supply alongside existing DRAM, HBM, and foundry partnerships.

bullets.title: AI safety guardrails slowing enterprise agent development; founders report week-long task delays
bullets.body: Multiple founders building agentic applications report that post-'cyber guardrails' implementation, American AI model progress has 'screeched to a halt' — tasks previously completed in one day now taking a week or more. Hedgeye notes the US government's new 'Gold Eagle' initiative requires explicit approval for frontier model releases, adding regulatory friction to the AI development cycle.

bullets.title: China deploys $9B 'National Team' buying to halt domestic equity selloff
bullets.body: China accelerated efforts to stabilize its domestic equity markets, deploying two major state funds and purchasing nearly $9B in shares. China also vowed to meet its annual economic targets per state media CCTV.

bullets.title: Semis underperformed S&P by ~840 bps last week — worst since 2009; KOSPI -28.5% from highs
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs notes semiconductors underperformed the S&P 500 by ~840 bps last week, the largest weekly underperformance since 2009, with July tracking as the worst month for semis since September 2001. South Korea's KOSPI fell another 4.5% overnight, now down 28.5% from recent highs, adding pressure to the semiconductor complex. HFs were reported dumping 'Anti-AI' quality factors while long-only funds were bidding semis, hardware, and storage.

bullets.title: JPM: Q2 earnings on pace for record buybacks; equal-weight S&P outperforming by ~5% since May lows
bullets.body: JPM notes US Q2 earnings are tracking +22% y/y with S&P 500 companies on pace to exceed $1.1T in share buybacks (record). Market breadth is improving, with S&P 500 equal-weight outperforming cap-weight by ~5% since May lows. 95% of first-week financial reporters beat EPS estimates vs. a 72% historical median.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 quality factor rotation: profitable stocks outperforming non-profitable YTD 2026
bullets.body: Profitable Russell 2000 companies are outperforming non-profitable ones in 2026 YTD, reversing the 2025 trend where non-profitable stocks outperformed by +20% vs +10%. This signals a quality/risk-off rotation within small caps.

bullets.title: ORCL data center costs surge $8B on Project Jupiter; CDS hitting all-time highs
bullets.body: Oracle's Project Jupiter power system costs increased to ~$8B, likely several billion above the original plan due to a fuel cell switch, per Morgan Stanley. Oracle is also reportedly facing broader cost overruns and delays at AI data center developments, with its CDS reaching new all-time highs.

bullets.title: HUT $9.8B Beacon Point lease + IREN $2.8B new contracts signal AI compute infrastructure acceleration
bullets.body: HUT fully commercialized its 1GW Beacon Point AI data center with a second 352MW lease worth $9.8B over 15 years (rising to $50.2B with renewals), redesigning the first data hall around Nvidia's architecture to increase capacity 57% in the same footprint. IREN simultaneously disclosed $2.8B in new customer contracts with leading AI developers, formally raising its 2026 annualized AI Cloud revenue target from $3.7B to $4.0B+.

bullets.title: South Korea hikes 25 bps (first since 2023); SoftBank overtakes Toyota as Japan's largest company
bullets.body: South Korea raised rates by 25 bps to 2.75%, its first hike since 2023, signaling continued global monetary tightening outside the US. Separately, SoftBank has overtaken Toyota as Japan's largest company by market cap — only the second time on record and the first since the peak of the 2000 tech bubble, reflecting AI/tech re-rating dynamics.

bullets.title: Stripe/Advent bid $60.50/sh for PayPal; Uber acquires Delivery Hero for €12.5B
bullets.body: M&A activity picked up with Stripe and Advent International submitting a joint offer to acquire PayPal at $60.50/share, and Uber offering to acquire Delivery Hero for €41.50/share in cash (~€12.5B deal). EU antitrust regulators also set to approve PIF consortium's acquisition of Electronic Arts.

bullets.title: TXN earnings catalyst: data center +90% YoY; UBS sees potential high-end/above guidance beat
bullets.body: TXN reports this week with consensus at $5.25B revenue and $1.94 EPS; UBS estimates $5.35B/$2.01 and sees TXN potentially guiding Q3 revenue ~$5.9B vs Street at $5.5-5.6B (+10% Q/Q vs normal seasonal 5-7%). TXN has beaten EPS consensus 18 of the past 20 quarters and is +22.3% since April 22 vs S&P +4.8%. Options imply ~9.8% move.
